body:
### Summary

When `/v1/querybatch` answers `200` with fewer `results` than the queries it was sent, `uv audit` pairs queries with results by position and silently drops the unmatched queries. The packages whose results are missing are never checked, but the command prints `Found no known vulnerabilities …` and exits `0`. A truncated or empty `200` body — from an intermediary proxy, a captive portal that happens to return JSON, or a service-side bug — therefore turns into a green audit.

### Reproduction (uv 0.12.21)

`pyproject.toml`:

```toml
[project]
name = "repro"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = ["python-multipart==0.0.6"]
```

`fake_osv.py`, an OSV stand-in that answers `200` with `N` fewer results than queries:

```python
import json, sys
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
    def do_POST(self):
        n = len(json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"])))["queries"])
        body = json.dumps({"results": [{}] * max(n - int(sys.argv[2]), 0)}).encode()
        self.send_response(200); self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body))); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(body)

HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", int(sys.argv[1])), H).serve_forever()
```

```console
$ uv lock
$ uv audit --frozen --preview-features audit-command                     # real OSV
  ...
  Advisory information: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-40347
$ echo $?
1

$ python3 fake_osv.py 18777 1 &                                          # one result short
$ uv audit --frozen --preview-features audit-command --service-url http://127.0.0.1:18777
Found no known vulnerabilities and no adverse project statuses in 1 package
$ echo $?
0

$ python3 fake_osv.py 18778 999 &                                        # {"results": []}
$ uv audit --frozen --preview-features audit-command --service-url http://127.0.0.1:18778
Found no known vulnerabilities and no adverse project statuses in 1 package
$ echo $?
0
```

Also reproduced on 0.12.9 and 0.12.19.

### Expected

A response whose `results` length differs from the number of queries in the batch is an error (exit `2`, like other service failures), not a clean result.

### Where

`crates/uv-audit/src/service/osv.rs`, `query_identifiers`, on `main`:

```rust
pending_batch.iter().zip(batch_response.results.iter())
```

`zip` stops at the shorter side. A length check before it (`batch_response.results.len() == pending_batch.len()`, otherwise an error) would close this. OSV's API documents one result per query, in order.

### Why it matters

`uv audit` is typically used as a CI gate or a scheduled check, where a false "clean" is the one failure nobody looks at. We found this while hardening a nightly audit job and currently guard against it with a known-vulnerable canary lock that must come back vulnerable before the real locks are trusted.
title: `uv audit` reports "no known vulnerabilities" (exit 0) when the OSV querybatch response has fewer results than queries
